items.claim: “Unplaced. Reported as putative polysporangiophytes, probably non-vascular”
items.evidence: The original proposes nonvascular polysporangiophytes; the review rejects confident land-plant assignment.
items.source: [Salamon et al. 2018](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.15091), full text; [Wellman et al. 2022](https://doi.org/10.1144/SP532-2022-92), full text.

items.claim: “first: Hirnantian”; “last: Hirnantian”; “445.2 to 443.1 Ma”; “c. 445 Ma on ICS v2016/12”
items.evidence: ICS confirms both boundaries; Salamon reports approximately 445 Ma using the older chart. These date deposition, not necessarily organismal occurrence.
items.source: [ICS v2024/12](https://stratigraphy.org/ICSchart/ChronostratChart2024-12.pdf), complete chart; [Salamon et al. 2018](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.15091), full text.

items.claim: “dated by trilobites, brachiopods and palynomorphs”; “confirmed by acritarchs and chitinozoans”
items.evidence: Both statements occur explicitly in the main article; the underlying sample-level supplementary evidence remains inaccessible.
items.source: [Salamon et al. 2018](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.15091), full text. Notes S1 download returned HTTP 403; its contents were not verified.

items.claim: “redeposited Cambrian to Middle Ordovician taxa such as Frankea”; fragments “could be redeposited and older than the Hirnantian”
items.section: Front matter: range.notes; Age and distribution
items.evidence: Frankea is specifically Middle Ordovician; older acritarchs demonstrate reworking. Trela explicitly allows older, redeposited plant fragments without demonstrating that origin.
items.source: [Trela et al. 2019](https://journals.pan.pl/Content/116562/PDF/82-85%20Trela_Czytelnia_ang.pdf), full text; [Trela and Szczepanik 2009](https://www.pgi.gov.pl/images/stories/przeglad/pg_2009_02_21.pdf), English abstract and relevant full-text sections.

items.claim: “fragments are 1.1 to 3.2 mm long, two of them broken at both ends”
items.evidence: Reported fragment lengths span these values; both Hostinella axes are incomplete.
items.source: [Salamon et al. 2018](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.15091), full text, description and Fig. 2.

items.section: Front matter: traits.axis_diameter_mm; Morphology table, Fig. 2a–c
items.evidence: All three dimension pairs match; measurements are widths, not demonstrated cylindrical diameters.
items.source: [Salamon et al. 2018](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.15091), full text, description.

items.claim: “two dichotomous axes placed in the form genus Hostinella and one trichotomous division”
items.evidence: Figures 2a–c and their descriptions match these counts and identifications.
items.source: [Salamon et al. 2018](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.15091), full text.

items.claim: “The 1.5 mm fertile axis is described as leafless”; “terminal on three fertile fragments”
items.evidence: Figure 2d is leafless; three putatively fertile specimens bear terminal bodies.
items.source: [Salamon et al. 2018](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.15091), full text, Fig. 2d–f.

items.claim: “One probable stoma, 29 x 21 µm, on an indeterminate dispersed axis”
items.evidence: Dimensions and indeterminate-axis attribution match; attachment to fertile specimens is not documented.
items.source: [Salamon et al. 2018](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.15091), full text, Fig. 3.

items.claim: “Rare trilete-like spores resembling Ambitisporites avitus-dilutus occur in the macerated residue, not in situ”
items.evidence: Residue spores are rare; irregular marks explicitly undermine their trilete identification.
items.source: [Salamon et al. 2018](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.15091), full text.

items.claim: “1.5 x 0.2”; “terminal bodies 0.4 x 0.3”
items.evidence: Both dimension pairs match the description.
items.source: [Salamon et al. 2018](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.15091), full text.

items.evidence: These axis and terminal-body measurements match the text.
items.source: [Salamon et al. 2018](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.15091), full text.

items.claim: “no spores inside the sporangium-like bodies, no conducting cells and no cuticle on the figured axes”
items.evidence: None is reported; this establishes reporting absence, not demonstrated biological absence.
items.source: [Salamon et al. 2018](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.15091), full text; supporting information inaccessible.

items.claim: “Marine shelf mudstone deposited during the Hirnantian regression”; “about 30 to 40 degrees S”
items.evidence: Trela describes marine deposition during regression and places the Holy Cross Mountains at 30–40°S near southwestern Baltica.
items.source: [Trela et al. 2019](https://journals.pan.pl/Content/116562/PDF/82-85%20Trela_Czytelnia_ang.pdf), full text; authors’ explanatory account.

items.claim: “lack sufficient characters to be assigned to land plants”
items.evidence: The review explicitly cites Salamon among insufficiently diagnostic claims; it does not establish an alternative identity for Zbrza.
items.source: [Wellman et al. 2022](https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/id/eprint/194499/1/SP532-2022-92.pdf), full text, plant-megafossil discussion.

items.claim: “449.65 Ma”; “soft maximum … 431.2 Ma”; “crown embryophytes at 457–450 Ma and crown tracheophytes at 432–428 Ma”
items.evidence: Main text confirms the numerical constraints and estimates; inaccessible Supplementary Table 4 prevents verification of the specified soft-maximum justification.
items.source: [Hooper et al. 2026](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41477-026-02432-3), full main text; Supplementary Information download failed.

items.claim: “record-timing”; “the one claimed macrofossil first appearance … earlier … by about 10 to 18 Myr”
items.evidence: Entire-stage bounds give approximately 10.2–18.5 Myr. This is an illustrative envelope, not a measured gap; the review lists multiple pre-Silurian claims.
items.source: [ICS v2024/12](https://stratigraphy.org/ICSchart/ChronostratChart2024-12.pdf), complete chart; [Wellman et al. 2022](https://doi.org/10.1144/SP532-2022-92), full text.

items.claim: “A single disputed record at Hirnantian … Zalesie Formation, Zbrza, Poland”; “probability class: disputed, low”
items.section: Model transfer: Can transfer, first bullet
items.evidence: One locality-level claim is documented. Neither source supplies a probability; an ordinal assessment should be called a confidence class.
items.source: [Salamon et al. 2018](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.15091), full text; [Wellman et al. 2022](https://doi.org/10.1144/SP532-2022-92), full text.

items.claim: “enter the base data set with no weight”; “enter a sensitivity scenario in which it is true”
items.section: Model transfer: Can transfer, first bullet
items.evidence: These are modelling prescriptions. No cited study evaluates this weighting rule or demonstrates its consequences for a first-appearance posterior.
items.source: [Wellman et al. 2022](https://doi.org/10.1144/SP532-2022-92), full text; supports identification uncertainty, not a particular statistical treatment.

items.claim: “worked false-positive case: tiny forking axes with terminal bodies, from marine mudstone, without in situ spores or attached conducting tissue”
items.section: Model transfer: Can transfer, second bullet
items.evidence: The observations support a disputed-identification example; the review does not demonstrate that Zbrza is a false positive.
items.source: [Salamon et al. 2018](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.15091), full text; [Wellman et al. 2022](https://doi.org/10.1144/SP532-2022-92), full text.

items.claim: “The model can use it to set a misidentification rate for records of this kind.”
items.section: Model transfer: Can transfer, second bullet
items.evidence: Neither source supplies validated classification outcomes or a sampling denominator. One unresolved assemblage cannot identify a population misidentification rate.
items.source: [Wellman et al. 2022](https://doi.org/10.1144/SP532-2022-92), full text; statistical identifiability assessment is the auditor’s inference.

items.claim: “Its dated stratigraphic position as a minimum age, whether or not the fragments are reworked.”
items.section: Model transfer: Can transfer, third bullet
items.evidence: Older reworking preserves a minimum constraint only if incorporation is genuine. Younger intrusion invalidates it; stage boundaries are not specimen dates.
items.source: [Trela et al. 2019](https://journals.pan.pl/Content/116562/PDF/82-85%20Trela_Czytelnia_ang.pdf), full text; minimum-age conditions are the auditor’s inference.

items.claim: “A confident first appearance of polysporangiophytes, tracheophytes, embryophytes, stomata, sporangia or trilete spores” cannot transfer
items.section: Model transfer: Cannot transfer, first bullet
items.evidence: Uncertain biological identification and possible reworking preclude these confident first-appearance assignments; an occurrence would still only constrain an earlier origin.
items.source: [Wellman et al. 2022](https://doi.org/10.1144/SP532-2022-92), full text; [Trela et al. 2019](https://journals.pan.pl/Content/116562/PDF/82-85%20Trela_Czytelnia_ang.pdf), full text. Origin-versus-occurrence distinction is an inference.

items.claim: “Any trait”; “Every trait … unknown”; “A whole-plant reconstruction, a height, a habit or a habitat”; comparisons “rest on shape”
items.section: Model transfer: Cannot transfer, second and third bullets
items.evidence: Whole-organism inference is unsupported, but specimen observations remain usable. Comparisons include size and structure; depositional setting differs from source habitat.
items.source: [Salamon et al. 2018](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.15091), full text; [Pacyna and Barbacka 2022](https://doi.org/10.5586/asbp.9123), full text, §2.1. Local front matter uses null size bounds and unknown categorical states.

items.claim: “the record is defended on shape alone”
items.evidence: The defence also invokes a possible stoma and excludes several animal alternatives.
items.source: [Salamon et al. 2018](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.15091), full text.

omissions: Salamon explicitly recognises three different fertile morphologies. Assemblage-wide association cannot establish that the axes, putative stoma and dispersed spores belong to one species. [Full text](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.15091).

The card’s shape-alone assessment omits the authors’ anatomical argument when drawing its conclusion. That argument can be challenged without erasing it. [Salamon et al., full text](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.15091).

The ICS boundaries each have ±0.9 Myr uncertainty. A numerical minimum should incorporate host-horizon uncertainty; 445.2 Ma is not a justified hard minimum. [Complete ICS chart](https://stratigraphy.org/ICSchart/ChronostratChart2024-12.pdf).

Wellman distinguishes demonstrated non-plant identifications from insufficiently diagnostic records and places Zbrza in the latter category. It supplies no confirmed false-positive label or rate. [Full text](https://doi.org/10.1144/SP532-2022-92).

Reworking affects temporal and geographical attribution even when biological identification is correct. Trela’s alternative transport routes therefore require separate treatment from taxonomic misidentification. [Full text](https://journals.pan.pl/Content/116562/PDF/82-85%20Trela_Czytelnia_ang.pdf).
model_transfer_assessment: Record-timing is an appropriate contrast, provided Zbrza remains an unresolved occurrence claim. The measurements concern separate Zbrza specimens, not a securely identified species; the putative stoma and dispersed spores cannot supply characters for the fertile fragments. Exclusion from a baseline and inclusion in a sensitivity analysis are defensible proposed choices, but neither the ordinal confidence label nor this single assemblage estimates a misidentification rate. The cannot-transfer limits mostly identify the biological uncertainties correctly, although they unnecessarily exclude specimen-level observations and blur depositional setting with source habitat. Minimum-age use must be conditional on genuine incorporation into the dated sediment and must propagate age uncertainty. Misidentification, older reworking and younger contamination need distinct observation processes.
overall: The card accurately reproduces most measurements and fairly records the published identification dispute. Its main weaknesses are calling Zbrza a usable false-positive calibration, overstating a shape-only defence, and insufficiently qualifying minimum-age transfer; the inaccessible supplements leave sample-level dating and processing evidence unverified.
